Vs
State and another------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
Khondker Musa Khaled J : On an application under section 561A of the of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the proceedings of the DAG GR No. 13 2002 arising out of Khulshi Police Station Case No. 41 dated 30-6-2002 under sections 420/120B/467/470/471/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, should not be quashed and/or pass such other order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Pending hearing of the rule, all further proceedings of the above mentioned FIR case were stayed. 

 3. Facts necessary for disposal of the rule are that the accused-petitioner Md Sadek Hossain was the Administrative Officer of Housing Estate, Chittagong, at the time of occurrence, and he also served in various positions at different working stations. He retired from service on 1-8-2006. On 30-6-2002, Md Rafiqul Islam, Inspector, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, lodged FIR, with Khulshi police station, Chittagong, alleging that the petitioner along with other three accused-persons committed offences under sections 420/120B/467/470/471/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption of Act, 1947 in connivance with each other by abusing official power. It has been alleged that plot No. 2/B, Lane-5, Road No. 2, Block-'K' measuring an area of 300 square feet of the Hali Shahar Housing Estate was illegally and fraudulently allotted to the accused Moklesur Rahman, father-in-law of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, Mr Md Hasan (accused No. 1) in the year 2000 violating order of the Ministry about prior approval. Previously the said plot was allotted to one Sultan Ahmed and after his death, Advocate Mahbubul instituted Title Suit No. 352 of 1986 and it was dismissed, and subsequently an appeal was preferred. When the Misc. Case No. 28 of 96, arising out of the Title Appeal, was pending, the accused-petitioners, in connivance with each other, cancelled the previous allotment given lawfully in favour of Sultan Ahmed and issued fresh allotment letter illegally in favour of the accused Muklesur Rahman, who was none but father-in-law of the accused No. 1 Md Hasan, the then Deputy Commissioner and Chairman of the Allotment committee of the said Housing Estate. It is also alleged in the FIR that the accused Moklesur Rahman submitted an application for allotment of the said plot, but before receiving the application, allotment letter was issued on 12-4-2000. The accused-petitioner being Administrative Officer and Member-Secretary of the Allotment Committee issued the allotment letter and executed lease agreement. That the accused-petitioner changed the resolution of the Meeting dated 10-8-2000 taken by the Housing Allotment Committee and manipulated the decision of the Committee by inserting the decision of allotting the plot to Moklesur Rahman. Two members of the Allotment Committee raised objection about the said illegally inserted decision,; and accordingly the matter was enquired into by the Anti-Corruption Bureau and when the prima-facie truth in the allegation was found by the preliminary enquiry, Inspector Mr Md Rafiqul Islam of Anti-Corruption Bureau lodged FIR against four accused-persons including the present petitioner on 30-6-2002. 

 4. When the case was under investigation, the accused No. 2 Md Sadek Hossain, retired Administrative Officer of the Housing Estate, preferred this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding and obtained the Rule and stay order. 

 5. Mr Jahirul Islam Mukul, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the learned filing Advocate Mr Md Harun-Or-Rashid, for the petitioner, submits that the allegations made out in the FIR against the accused-petitioner do not attract ingredients of the offences under sections 420/120B/467/470/471/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. It is submitted that the accused-petitioner was sub-ordinate officer of the principal accused Md Hasan, Deputy Corn missioner and Chairman, Plot Allotment Committee, and as such, he had to carry out the orders of the deputy Commissioner and he cannot be held liable to be prosecuted under any offence relating to such illegal allotment to Moklesur Rahman and others. It is submitted that the principal accused-persons of the case namely Md Hasan and Moklesur Rahman, his father-in-law, (beneficiary in getting allotment) have already succeeded in getting the impugned proceeding against them quashed in criminal Misc. Case No. 249 of 2003 and Criminal Misc. Case No. 13140 of 2005. In both the cases, the Rules were made absolute by the analogous judgment dated 23-5-2006. The Anti-Corruption Commission did not prefer any appeal against it. The learned Advocate further submits that since. the principal accused persons are not more accused in the case, it would be useless to continue the criminal case against others and the accused-petitioner should not suffer after retirement. It is submitted that the accused-petitioner could not get pension benefit due to this case. Accordingly, the learned Advocate has prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 6. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-party No. 2 Anti-Corruption Commission, submits, in reply, that the proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable as to cognizance has yet been taken against the accused-petitioner. He submits that when the investigation was going on, the accused-petitioner has initiated the instant quashing proceeding, as such it can not legally be sustained prior to the taking cognizance. In this respect, the learned Advocate has relied upon the case of Abdul Haque vs State reported in 60 DLR (AD) 1. Next he submits that there are specific allegations against the accused-petitioner to connect him with the offence and, as such, the question of quashing the FIR proceeding does not arise. 

 There is also allegation against the accused-petitioner to the effect that he cancelled previous valid allotment of Sultan Ahmed illegally, though a Civil Suit was pending over the matter. There is also allegation against the accused-petitioner that the allotment letter was issued in favour of accused Moklesur Rahman without approval of the Allotment Committee and concerned Ministry violating the rules. It has been further alleged that subsequently the accused-petitioners in connivance with each other, changed page No. 10 of the minutes of the meeting by inserting the decision of fresh allotment of plot in favour of Moklesur Rahman. On a plain reading of the FIR, it is evident that there are clear prima-facie allegations to attract at least some of the offences under the penal code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The accused-petitioner, being a government servant, cannot misuse his official position to provide advantage to another person illegally violating the decision of the concerned Ministry regarding allotment of plot. Therefore, it is not such a case that if the allegations as made out by the prosecution is the FIR are taken to be true, do not constitute any offence under the law. So, the principle of quashing a criminal proceeding is not available in this instant case." 

 8. It is true that the principal two accused-persons namely Md Hasan, Ex-Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong and his father-in-law Moklesur Rahman escaped from being prosecuted due to judgment passed in Criminal Misc. Case No. 249 of 2003 and criminal Case No. 13140 of 2005. Both the Rules are invade absolute by another Division bench of this Court by the said, judgment dated 23-5-2006. We have gone through the said judgment very carefully, but we are unable to agree with the finding that there is no prima-facie allegation against the accused-petitioner and other accused-persons for initiating any criminal proceeding. Moreover, disputed facts cannot be decided in the quashing proceeding as have been done. 

 9. Over and above, decision of the Appellate Division given in the case of Abdul Huque vs State reported in 60 DLR (AD) 1 has, not been considered at all by the High Court Division in those cases. 

 "Before taking of cognisance of a case by the competent court or tribunal a proceedings cannot be said to be pending and accordingly, a proceeding cannot be quashed unless cognisance in respect  thereof has been taken and process issued." 

 11. In view of the aforesaid decision of our apex Court, no case can be subject matter of quashment before submission of the charge-sheet and cognizance is taken there under. In fact, a criminal case starts from the stage of taking cognizance. Unless cognizance is taken, the FIR named suspected persons are not accused before the court in the eye of law. So, when no criminal case exists before the date of taking cognizance, the question of quashing such a non-existent criminal case by invoking section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not arise at all. In such view of the matter, we cannot, agree with the judgment passed by another Division Bench in the matter of quashing the impugned criminal proceeding before, taking cognizance. The view taken by the Appellate Division in 60 DLR (AD) 1 being the latest, has got binding effect on the High Court Division; and, as such, we are led to hold that the impugned proceeding (FIR case), not being a regular criminal proceeding in the eye of law, cannot be quashed during investigation period. 

 12. In the case of Bangladesh vs AT Mridha reported in 26 DLR (SC) 17, it has held that section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be utilised to quash an investigation work of the police. So, the impugned proceeding is not liable to be quashed, on this ground as well. 

 13. Considering all aspects of the case and legal position, we are of the view that the Rule issued in this case has no substance ankle as such, it is not legally sustainable. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is discharged. Stay order passed in connection with this Rule stands vacated. The Investigating Officer is directed to submit police report as early as possible for expeditious disposal of the case.
